title: 2020年12月四级真题 第3套 阅读2
paperTitle: 2020年12月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
passage:
P1 The terms "global warming" and "climate change" are used by many, seemingly interchangeably. But do they really mean the same thing?

P2 Scientists shaped the history of the terms while attempting to accurately describe how humans continue to alter the planet. Later, political strategists adopted the terms to influence public opinion.

P3 In 1975, geochemist Wallace Broecker introduced the term "climate change" in an article published by Science. In 1979, a National Academy of Sciences report used the term "global warming" to define increases in the Earth's average surface temperature, while "climate change" more broadly referred to the numerous effects of this increase, such as sea-level rise and ocean acidification(酸化).

P4 During the following decades, some industrialists and politicians launched a campaign to sow doubt in the minds of the American public about the ability of fossil-fuel use, deforestation and other human activities to influence the planet's climate.

P5 Word use played a critical role in developing that doubt. For example, the language and polls expert Frank Luntz wrote a memo encouraging the use of "climate change" because the phrase sounded less scary than "global warming," reported the Guardian.

P6 However, Luntz's recommendation wasn't necessary. A Google Ngram Viewer chart shows that by 1993 climate change was already more commonly used in books than global warming. By the end of the next decade both words were used more frequently, and climate change was used nearly twice as often as global warming.

P7 NASA used the term "climate change" because it more accurately reflects the wide range of changes to the planet caused by increasing amounts of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.

P8 The debate isn't new. A century ago, chemist Svante Arrhenius started one of the first debates over the potential for humans to influence the planet's climate. Arrhenius calculated the capability of carbon dioxide to trap heat in the Earth's atmosphere, but other chemists disagreed. Some argued that humans weren't producing enough greenhouse gases, while others claimed the effects would be tiny. Now, of course, we know that whatever you call it, human behavior is warming the planet, with grave consequences ahead.

questions.q: Why did politicians use the two terms "global warming" and "climate change"?
options: To sway public opinion of the impact of human activities on Earth.
To more accurately describe the consequences of human activities.
To win more popular votes in their campaign activities.
To assure the public of the safety of existing industries.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why did politicians use the two terms 问的是政客使用这两个词的具体原因，属对文中明 示原因的事实性提问。

【拆句】题干 Why did politicians use the two terms "global warming" and "climate change"? 主干是 "Why did politicians use the two terms"，引号里的两个术语只是 the two terms 的同位补充，句式平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】Later, political strategists adopted the terms to influence public opinion. 后来，政治策略家们采用这些术语，是为了影响公众舆论。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 to influence public opinion ↔To sway public opinion how humans continue to alter the planet ↔the impact of human activities on Earth 把 to influence public opinion 改成 To sway public opinion 再叠加上文 "how humans alter the planet" 的名词化转述，正好等价于 To sway public opinion of the impact of human activities on Earth.。 B) 张冠李戴 To more accurately describe the consequences of human activities. 这是 Scientists shaped the history of the terms while attempting to accurately describe how humans continue to alter the planet. 里科学家的目的，被错配到政客 头上。 C) 无中生有 To win more popular votes in their campaign activities. 文章只字未提选举或拉票； launched a campaign 中的 campaign 指"运动"而非"竞选活动"。 D) 与原文相反 To assure the public of the safety of existing industries. 与原文相反——launched a campaign to sow doubt 表明政客是制造怀疑、并非给公众吃定心丸。 在美国国家科学院报告中使用的"气候变化"一词与"全球变暖"的不同之处在于_________。 A) 听起来不那么模糊 B) 看起来更科学 C) 涵盖更多现象 D) 更接近现实

questions.q: As used in a National Academy of Sciences report, the term "climate change" differs from "global
options: it is much closer to reality
questions.explain:
【判型】As used in a National Academy of Sciences report, the term "climate change" differs from "global warming" in that_________. 问的是该报告里两词的具体差异，属事实层 提问。 52. As used in a National Academy of Sciences report, the term "climate change" differs from "global warming" in that_________. A) it sounds less vague B) it looks more scientific C) it covers more phenomena D) it is much closer to reality

【拆句】题干 As used in a National Academy of Sciences report, the term "climate change" differs from "global warming" in that_________. 是个待补全的陈述句，主干 "the term climate change differs from global warming in that ..."，As 引导的状语限定范围；空格 由 in that 引导的从句填，选项即从句内容。

【定位】In 1979, a National Academy of Sciences report used the term "global warming" to define increases in the Earth's average surface temperature, while "climate change" more broadly referred to the numerous effects of this increase, such as sea-level rise and ocean acidification(酸化). 1979 年，美国国家科学院的一份报告用 global warming 这个术语来指地球地表平均温度 的上升，而 climate change 则更广泛地指这一升温带来的诸多影响，例如海平面上升和海 洋酸化。

【选项】A) 答非所问 it sounds less vague 谈的是"听起来更不含糊"，可这个报告本身比较的是两术语的指代 范围，不是听感；听感是 P5 里 Luntz 的话题，与本题报告无关。 B) 无中生有 it looks more scientific 谈"显得更科学"，原文从未比较两术语的科学性观感，纯属 编造。 C) ✓ 正确 more broadly referred to the numerous effects ↔it covers more phenomena 预判已经定调"climate change 范围更宽"，四个选项里只有 it covers more phenomena 直接讲范围差异，与定位句中 more broadly + numerous effects 一一 对位。 D) 无中生有 it is much closer to reality 说"更贴近现实"，原文并未在该报告中比较两术语谁更接近 实际，是无中生有。 20世纪末的实业家采取了什么手段来误导美国人? A) 编造的调查结果。 B) 虚假的研究发现。 C) 雇用气候专家。 D) 刻意选择措辞。

questions.q: What did industrialists of the late 20th century resort to in order to mislead Americans?
questions.explain:
【判型】What did industrialists of the late 20th century resort to in order to mislead Americans? 问的是实业家采取的具体手段，属对文中明示信息的事实性提问。 53. What did industrialists of the late 20th century resort to in order to mislead Americans? A) Made-up survey results. B) False research findings. C) Hired climate experts. D) Deliberate choice of words.

【拆句】题干 What did industrialists of the late 20th century resort to in order to mislead Americans? 主干 "What did industrialists resort to"，of the late 20th century 修饰 industrialists，in order to mislead Americans 是目的状语；resort to 意为"诉诸于"，是 高频四级词组。

【定位】Word use played a critical role in developing that doubt. For example, the language and polls expert Frank Luntz wrote a memo encouraging the use of "climate change" because the phrase sounded less scary than "global warming," reported the Guardian. 用词起到了关键作用，造就了那种怀疑。例如，语言与民调专家 Frank Luntz 写了一份备忘 录，建议使用 climate change，因为它听起来不像 global warming 那么吓人——《卫 报》报道。

【选项】A) 无中生有 Made-up survey results. 说"伪造调查结果"，原文只字未提调查造假，纯属编造。 B) 无中生有 False research findings. 说"虚假的研究发现"，原文从未提及实业家发布假研究，只提 了使用词汇上的策略。 C) 张冠李戴 Hired climate experts. 把 the language and polls expert Frank Luntz 的身份错置 ——Luntz 是语言与民调专家，并非气候专家，且原文未说他被实业家雇佣。 D) ✓ 正确 Word use played a critical role in developing that doubt. ↔Deliberate choice of words. 预判已明确"在用词上做手脚"，四个选项里只有 Deliberate choice of words. 谈选词， 其他三个分别引到调查、研究、专家，都不是文中点出的手段。 NASA为什么选择"气候变化"这个术语? A) 为了获得更多资金。 B) 为了更精确。 C) 出于政治需要。 D) 为了避免争论。

questions.q: Why did NASA choose the term "climate change"?
questions.explain:
【判型】Why did NASA choose the term "climate change"? 是 Why 提问，问 NASA 选这个术 语的原因，原文必有直接对应句。

【拆句】题干 Why did NASA choose the term "climate change"? 是简单疑问句，主干 "Why did NASA choose the term"，引号短语作 choose 的宾语，句式无陷阱。 54. Why did NASA choose the term "climate change"? A) To obtain more funds. B) For greater precision. C) For political needs. D) To avoid debate.

【定位】NASA used the term "climate change" because it more accurately reflects the wide range of changes to the planet caused by increasing amounts of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. 美国国家航空航天局之所以使用 climate change 这个术语，是因为它能更准确地反映由大 气中温室气体增加所引发的地球范围广泛的变化。

【选项】A) 无中生有 To obtain more funds. 谈"获取更多资金"，原文从未提及 NASA 的预算或经费问题。 B) ✓ 正确 more accurately reflects ↔For greater precision 预判已经给出"为了更准确"这个核心，四个选项里只有 For greater precision 谈精准 度，其他三个引到资金、政治、避免争论，都没在 P7 中出现过。 C) 张冠李戴 For political needs. 谈"出于政治需要"，这是 political strategists 与 industrialists and politicians 的动机，而非 NASA 的；NASA 的选词理由是科学准确性。 D) 无中生有 To avoid debate. 说"为了避免争论"，原文 P7 只字未提 NASA 想回避争论；P8 反而表 明争论一直存在、不可回避。 作者的最终结论是什么? A) 全球变暖是更准确的术语。 B) 术语的准确性在科学中很重要。 C) 人类活动对地球有严重影响。 D) 政治干扰严肃的科学辩论。

questions.q: What is the author's final conclusion?
options: Global warming is the more accurate term.
Accuracy of terminology matters in science.
Human activities have serious effects on Earth.
Politics interferes with serious scientific debate.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the author's final conclusion? 问的是作者的最终结论，是对全文中心的提问，不 靠某一句的细节解决。

【拆句】题干 What is the author's final conclusion? 是 What is 句型，主干极简，author's final 是 conclusion 的双层修饰，提示找全文末尾的总结表态。 55. What is the author's final conclusion? A) Global warming is the more accurate term. B) Accuracy of terminology matters in science. C) Human activities have serious effects on Earth. D) Politics interferes with serious scientific debate.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 Global warming is the more accurate term. 说 global warming 更准确，恰好和 NASA used the term "climate change" because it more accurately reflects the wide range of changes 与 whatever you call it 的立场相反。 B) 以偏概全 Accuracy of terminology matters in science. 把"术语精确度"当作全文主旨，但这只 是 P3、P7 这两个局部所谈，作者在末段已明确越过术语之争，落点在"人类影响"。 C) ✓ 正确 human behavior is warming the planet, with grave consequences ahead ↔ Human activities have serious effects on Earth. Human activities have serious effects on Earth. 既概括了 P8 末句的核心判断，也 覆盖前文 P3 提到的海平面上升、海洋酸化等具体后果，是唯一兼顾主线与全文铺垫的 选项。 D) 以偏概全 Politics interferes with serious scientific debate. 说"政治干预严肃科学辩论"，这只是 P4\~P5 局部话题，且原文未给出"干预了严肃科学辩论"这样的明确价值判断，更不是作 者最终结论。
